issues.display_title: Issue #226: Stitching: remove the batch time estimate
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

The Stitch 360 batch header showed a time estimate ("~Xm left") while a batch was running. The number was a guess: the first panorama was paced off a 108 s figure measured on one Windows box at one image size, and later ones off the session's running average. On other machines or resolutions it was misleading, so it is removed.

  • Branch: design/update-layout-panorama-frame-planner

What changed

The header now shows the summary (N panoramas · N photos) and the overall progress bar only.

Everything that existed only to feed the estimate is removed with it:

  • QueueBoard.tsx — the ETA line and its calculation.
  • hooks/useStitching.ts — per-panorama start/finish timing (startedAtRef, durations) and avgItemSeconds.
  • utils/progress.ts — etaRemainingSeconds, formatDuration, averageItemSeconds, DEFAULT_ITEM_SECONDS, plus their tests in progress.test.mjs.
  • src/locales/en.json — t_stitching.t_eta_remaining (no other locale had it).

Unchanged

  • The per-card step chip still shows elapsed seconds for the running step. It counts up, it is not an estimate.
  • The eased per-card progress bar (interpolatedProgress, measured step seconds) is untouched.

Verification

  • pnpm typecheck passes
  • progress.test.mjs passes (12/12)
  • Manual: run a Stitch 360 batch, header shows no "left" text, progress bar still advances

DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

New Edit tool: take one equirectangular panorama, plan N vertical "frames" around the 360° circle, and export each frame as a JPEG. Ported from the reference web tool Panorama Projection Planner v9.1 onto the GoThru architecture (RTK slice + Content/Settings + hook + Rust image crate command), using the Crop feature as the template throughout.

This is not a reprojection. A frame is a column crop of equirect pixels with wrap at the 0°/360° seam, so wide frames keep the characteristic equirect curvature — deliberately uncorrected.

  • Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-panorama-frame-planner-design.md
  • Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-07-panorama-frame-planner.md
  • Branch: design/update-layout-panorama-frame-planner

Confirmed decisions

# Decision Choice
1 Frame projection Equirect column-crop, not rectilinear
2 Aspect ratio Presets — 4:5 default, 1:1, 3:2, 16:9, custom
3 Output Subfolder <dir>/frame-planner/ + reload in preview; EXIF/XMP/ICC copied from source
4 Circular groups + snap Ported in full (links[]/components() BFS + edge snap)
5 Export modes Both — exact frame regions, and gap-free tiled full panorama
6 Access Free, no requirePro gate
7 Name / key Panorama Frame Planner / editMenu: 'panorama-frame-planner'

Scope

New frontend: features/edit/framePlanner/ (frameLayout.ts pure math, framePlannerSlice.ts, layoutFile.ts + tests) and components/features/Edit/FramePlanner/ (Content, Settings, constants, framePlannerUtils, hooks/).

Modified frontend: types/viewer.ts (editMenu union), types/edit.ts, editReducer.ts, Edit/Menu.tsx, Edit/Edit.tsx, lib/ipc.ts, locales/en.json, docs/migration/00-ipc-inventory.md.

Backend: new src-tauri/src/commands/frame_planner.rs (frame_planner_export, frame_planner_save_layout), registered in commands/mod.rs + lib.rs generate_handler! and allowed in capabilities/*.json. No new binaries — image crate only, with exiftool for metadata copy.

issues.display_title: Issue #221: feat(edit): confirm before starting a second job while another is running
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Starting a second Edit job while another one is still running silently splits CPU and RAM between them, so both runs get slower with no warning — a user who kicks off Enfuse while a Stitch 360 batch is mid-flight just sees everything crawl.

Every Edit tool now asks first: "Another process is still running — Cancel / Continue anyway". The prompt names the tool already running and the one being started, and the job only begins after Continue.

  • Branch: design/update-layout-panorama-frame-planner

How it works

No new job registry. Who is busy is already in the store, so the check is a selector over state.edit:

Signal Tools
a logProcess item with status: 'Processing' the queue tools (stitching, enfuse, minify, resize, …)
the isGenerating flag Room Staging, 2D Virtual Stage, Object Remover — these never mark a log Processing

Both signals are needed: without isGenerating the three AI tools would never register as busy and the gate would silently pass while they run.

New files

  • src/renderer/features/edit/shared/busyFeatures.ts — selectBusyFeatures + slice-key → t_menu_edit.* label map (EDIT_FEATURE_LABEL_KEYS), typed EditFeatureKey.
  • src/renderer/features/edit/shared/concurrentGate.ts — confirmConcurrentStart(feature): Promise<boolean>. Resolves true immediately when nothing else runs, so the normal path costs nothing. Lives outside React so any hook can await it.
  • src/renderer/components/modals/ConcurrentProcessModal.tsx — HeroUI modal, mounted once in App.tsx, subscribes via useSyncExternalStore.
  • src/renderer/features/edit/shared/busyFeatures.test.mjs — 5 tests, including one asserting every label key resolves in en.json.

i18n — t_concurrent_process (t_title, t_description with {{running}} / {{started}}, t_cancel, t_continue) added to all 18 locale files.

Gate placement

18 call sites, all at the batch boundary next to trackEditGenerate. The gate always runs before the first queue item flips to Processing (and before isGenerating is set), so Cancel leaves the queue exactly as it was instead of stranding an item in Processing.

  • Stitch 360 — useStitching.ts
  • Enfuse — useEnfuseProcess.ts
  • Image Minifier — useMinifyJpgQueue.ts
  • Batch Resize — useImageResizeActions.tsx
  • Scale Up Image — useScaleUpImage.ts
  • Crop — useCrop.ts
  • Frame Planner — useFramePlanner.ts
  • Image Straightener — useImageStraightenerActions.ts
  • Auto Level — useAutoLevel.tsx (batch start + single-item retry)
  • Nadir Builder — useNadirBuilder.tsx
  • Logo Nadir Patching — useLogoPatching.tsx
  • AI Nadir Patching — useAiNadirPatching.tsx (batch start + retry)
  • Cube → Equirectangular — useCubeToEquirectangular.tsx
  • Equirectangular → Cube — useEquirectangularToCube.tsx
  • Virtual Staging 360 + 2D — useStagingSettings.ts
  • Object Remover — useObjectRemover.ts

Six start functions became async to await the prompt (startWith, startProcess, startQueue, startResize, startPatching, retryProcess); every caller ignores the return value, checked.

Deliberate limits

  • A second prompt raised while one is already open resolves false (the later start is refused) rather than queueing modals.
  • No unit test for concurrentGate itself — it imports the @store alias, which the node --test .mjs runner cannot resolve. Its core, selectBusyFeatures, is covered.

Verification status

  • pnpm typecheck — clean
  • pnpm test — 196/196 passing (59 suites)
  • eslint on every touched file — 0 errors (warnings are pre-existing: max-lines, unused vars, exhaustive-deps)

issues.display_title: Issue #220: Stitching: multiblend panorama is not 2:1
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

What is wrong

On Windows, stitching with the default blender (multiblend) produces a panorama that is not 2:1, so any spherical viewer maps rows to the wrong latitude. --blender enblend is unaffected.

Cause

multiblend has no equivalent of enblend's -f WxH, which the enblend branch has always passed. Both blenders default to writing the union of their inputs' bounding boxes, and nona's remapped tiles are each cropped to the pixels one frame covers. A 360 rig that sees no nadir therefore gets a panorama shorter than the canvas — an 8k stitch comes out 8192 wide but short of 4096 tall.

Measured on two cropped tiles with the bundled binaries:

Blender Args as the pipeline passes them Output
enblend --blend-colorspace=identity -w -f 400x200 400×200 (2.0)
multiblend --wideblend -w 400×120 (3.33)

Already fixed, not yet shipped to Windows

Fixed in GoThruMedia/fisheye-stitch@b2db7da: multiblend records where the union sat in the output's TIFF XPosition/YPosition, so the panorama is pasted back onto the full canvas afterwards. Verified end to end on 8 fisheye frames — --blender multiblend --size 4k now outputs 4096×2048.

The mac binary is already rebundled (8ffd099). The Windows .exe still predates the fix: it cannot be cross-built from macOS because the MSVC linker is not available there.

What to do

On a Windows machine:

  1. In fisheye-stitch, check out b2db7da or later and run cargo build --release.
  2. Copy target/release/fisheye-stitch.exe over src-tauri/binaries/win/fisheye-stitch/fisheye-stitch.exe.
  3. Verify: stitch a set with --blender multiblend --size 4k and confirm the output is 4096×2048.

Notes

  • The gpu blender was checked and is unaffected — it already composites onto the full canvas read from the project file.
  • The uncovered nadir is meant to stay in the canvas as a black gap; that is the correct result, not a defect.
